seo.title: Homeless help in Liverpool - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in Liverpool: emergency housing, outreach, food, health care, benefits, work and specialist support.

content.text: Immediate danger, serious illness, police, fire or ambulance:
Sleeping outside or nowhere safe tonight:
Always Help Available / No Second Night Out
Urgent but not life-threatening medical or mental-health help:

notice.text: Beds, meals, opening times and eligibility can change.
Call before travelling when possible. An assessment, outreach contact or referral does not guarantee accommodation. Never pay anyone who claims they can secure a council or charity place.

content.text: Tell the worker where you are tonight, where you usually sleep, your age, whether children are with you, and whether pregnancy, disability, illness, domestic abuse, immigration restrictions or a pet affects what is safe. If a service cannot help, ask for the next safe option and write down the advice.

Call for immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, fire or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first. If you cannot speak on a mobile call to police, listen and press 55 when prompted.

The hub has a confidential address and is accessed through the service: it is not a walk-in shelter and a bed is not guaranteed.

items.name: Register with a GP without an address or ID

content.text: You do not need proof of address, immigration status, identification or an NHS number to register with a GP. You can use a temporary address or the surgery's address with permission.
for severe pain, swelling, bleeding, infection or a broken tooth when you cannot get a dentist. Call 999 for swelling affecting breathing or swallowing or a major facial injury.

categories.title: 7. Toilets, internet, charging and warm spaces

content.text: Monday–Friday 9am–8pm and Saturday 9am–5pm; closed bank holidays. Free unlimited Wi-Fi does not require membership. Computers require free membership and are walk-up, subject to capacity.
Gender-neutral, accessible and Changing Places toilets are available. Printing costs money. Ask staff before charging a device.
Information Centre, 5 Wall Street, Liverpool L1 8JQ
Free toilets include accessible, stoma-friendly and changing facilities. Published hours are Monday–Friday 9am–8pm, Saturday 9am–7pm and Sunday 10:30am–5pm, with different bank-holiday hours.

All Liverpool libraries provide free Wi-Fi; computers, printing and photocopying are also available. Allerton, Garston, Norris Green and Speke Parklands can help with online council tasks. Not every branch has a public toilet.
Community Connect normally provides a warm indoor space, tea and coffee at Oakfield Road, L4 0UF, Tuesday–Thursday 10am–3pm during autumn and winter. Check the seasonal timetable.

Liverpool residents aged 16+ on a low income may receive short-term help after a sudden financial crisis. Possible help includes food, utilities, clothing, hygiene, furniture, travel, phone or internet and some rent shortfalls or housing costs. You do not have to receive benefits.
An award is not guaranteed. Urgent cases may be decided within 48 hours. Apply online, by phone, through a One Stop Shop or support organisation.

items.name: Universal Credit without a fixed address

content.text: You can claim while rough sleeping, sofa surfing or staying in a hostel. With permission, use a trusted person's, hostel, day-centre or Jobcentre address. If you lack ID, a bank account, phone, email or National Insurance number, say so: alternatives may be possible.
Tell your work coach about homelessness, mental ill health or recovery needs and ask whether your claimant commitment should change temporarily.
, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Free advice on benefits, housing, work, family, immigration, consumer problems and discrimination.

Housing Benefit can still apply to some hostel, supported, sheltered or council-arranged temporary accommodation even when other costs use Universal Credit. Ask the provider and council which claim is correct.

categories.title: 9. Work, training and travel to a new job

content.text: Free personalised employment help for Liverpool residents aged 18+, including skills, confidence, apprenticeships, work trials and one-to-one support. Connect to Work is for jobseekers facing additional barriers.

Use the official Find a Job service and postcode search for a current Jobcentre. Do not rely on an old office address. A Jobcentre can help with Universal Credit, work-coach appointments and National Insurance questions.
Free advice on CVs, interviews, qualifications, training and careers for adults in England. Ask for phone or online support if you cannot travel.

items.name: Life Rooms employment and learning help

content.text: for practical help with employment, learning, benefits and housing when wellbeing or mental health is also a barrier. It is not a recruitment agency or emergency service.

items.name: Travel, phone or essentials for work

content.text: The Crisis and Resilience Fund may help an eligible resident with travel, phone or internet costs during a sudden crisis. A Jobcentre work coach may consider the Flexible Support Fund for agreed work costs. Ask before paying; neither is automatic.

Check old payslips, benefit letters, a tax account or UKVI account first. You may start work before receiving a number if you can prove the right to work, and do not need one to start a benefit claim.
Apply for or find a number

British and Irish citizens may use an eligible passport or a birth or adoption certificate together with an official document showing their National Insurance number. Other people may use a share code or eligible immigration documents.
Do not pay an unofficial agent. Ask Citizens Advice or a regulated adviser if status is unclear.
Order through the General Register Office or relevant register office. Fees apply. Ask a support worker about safe delivery and possible fee help.
Contact HM Passport Office before paying if documents, referees or delivery are difficult. A charity may help you apply but cannot guarantee the fee.
Libraries provide free Wi-Fi, and Central Library has walk-up computers for members. The Crisis and Resilience Fund may assess phone or internet costs; equipment or credit is not guaranteed.

items.name: Adult social care, disability and safeguarding

content.text: . Call if illness, disability, injury, abuse, neglect or self-neglect affects an adult's daily living or safety. Call 999 for immediate danger.
Social care does not replace a homeless application. Contact both services if care needs affect safe accommodation.

Volunteer vets provide a monthly city-centre outreach clinic for pets belonging to people experiencing homelessness. Care can include checks, vaccinations, microchipping, parasite treatment, medication and pet essentials.
The public date and location are not fixed on the official page. Use the help form or ask Whitechapel. StreetVet is not an emergency service.

The UK-wide scheme helps eligible dog owners with veterinary costs and finding dog-friendly services. A participating homelessness service may need to apply. Assessment applies; existing bills and every procedure are not automatically covered.

items.name: Tell every service about your pet

content.text: Some placements accept pets and others do not. Tell the council and referrer the species, size, health, behaviour and vaccination status. Ask for a pet-friendly option before accepting or rejecting a placement.
Do not abandon an animal or arrive at an unknown hostel expecting admission.

categories.title: 15. Transport and Liverpool John Lennon Airport

content.text: Use the official planner and live updates for buses, trains and ferries. Ask a housing, health, council or Jobcentre worker before an appointment whether travel can be authorised; help is not automatic.
Queen Square Bus Station, L1 1RG, Monday–Saturday 8am–6:30pm and Sunday 10am–5pm.
Ask about routes, fares and tickets. Holiday hours can differ.
The Crisis and Resilience Fund may help an eligible resident with necessary bus fares during a sudden financial crisis. Apply before buying a ticket when possible.

items.name: Liverpool John Lennon Airport by bus

content.text: The 500 links Liverpool ONE and the airport about every 30 minutes; Arriva publishes a journey of about 30 minutes and service from around 4am to midnight. Routes 80A and 86A also connect the city, Liverpool South Parkway and airport.
Check the day's timetable and fare. The terminal is not accommodation; if stranded with nowhere safe, call

Liverpool South Parkway is the nearest main rail station. Continue by an 80A, 86A or other current airport bus. Some rail tickets can include the bus connection when the destination is Liverpool John Lennon Airport.
